content_list.content_text: The 2020s began with a celebration. On February 9, Parasite (2019) won the Oscar for Best Picture, the first ever for a non-English-language film, and cinema seemed more global and more alive than ever. A month later, the world stopped. On March 11, the World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a pandemic. China had already closed some 70,000 screens on January 23, the eve of the Lunar New Year, the most lucrative time of year for the country's theaters. Italy, France, Spain, the United States and Brazil followed within days. By mid-March, the two biggest American chains, AMC and Regal, had closed all their theaters. In more than a century of history, never had so many screens gone dark at the same time.

information.contentText: A movie theater in South Surrey, Canada, in April 2020. On the marquee, instead of the films now playing, a notice: the doors were temporarily closed for the health of the public and staff.

content_list.content_text: The first warning came even before the WHO's declaration. On March 4, the producers of No Time to Die (2021), Daniel Craig's farewell as James Bond, pushed its release from April to November 2020: it was the first major film to change dates because of the virus, and it would not be Bond's last delay. In Brazil, 577 screens had already gone dark by March 17. That same week, distributors canceled their releases, and on Thursday, March 19, for the first time in history, not a single film opened in the country's theaters. Cinemark, Kinoplex, Cinépolis, UCI and Espaço Itaú, Brazil's main theater chains, closed their doors with no date to reopen. According to Ancine, Brazil's national film agency, the country's moviegoing audience, which had reached 177.7 million admissions in 2019, plunged to 39.4 million in 2020.

Festivals had to reinvent themselves. The Cannes Film Festival, scheduled for May, at first tried to postpone its edition while part of the Palais des Festivals served as a temporary shelter for homeless people. In April, it admitted it would not take place “in its original form” and ended up announcing a selection under the Cannes 2020 label, with no competition and no Palme d'Or, something that had not happened since 1968. The Venice Film Festival was the first of the major festivals to return in person, from September 2 to 12, with mandatory masks, an empty seat between every two spectators, temperature checks at the entrance and a red carpet with no crowds. The Golden Lion went to Nomadland (2020), by Chloé Zhao. The film premiered on the same day in Venice, in Toronto and at a drive-in set up in the parking lot of the Rose Bowl stadium in California.

information.contentText: With the Telluride Film Festival canceled, the American premiere of Nomadland took place on September 11, 2020, at a drive-in at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena. The applause came in the form of honking horns and flashing headlights.

content_list.content_text: The Rose Bowl drive-in was not an isolated stopgap. With indoor theaters closed, a format that had seemed like a museum piece was back in fashion. In the United States, open-air theaters, where each family watches the movie from inside its own car, stayed open and became a hot ticket. In Brazil, the Cine Drive-in Brasília, opened in 1973 and one of the last survivors of its kind in the country, reopened on the May 1 holiday in 2020 at half capacity and sold 2,800 tickets that first weekend. In São Paulo, the Petra Belas Artes art house set up a 100-car drive-in at the Memorial da América Latina starting June 16, programming classics by Nolan and Stanley Kubrick. Similar initiatives sprang up in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais and in many other countries. The drive-in saved no one financially, but it became the symbol of an audience that wanted, by any means necessary, to watch movies together.

information.contentText: Aerial view of a drive-in in Cologne, Germany, in May 2020. In the middle of the pandemic, cars parked with plenty of room between them became the safest way to watch a movie as a group.

content_list.content_text: Amid the chaos, one filmmaker became the spokesman for the movie theater. Christopher Nolan wanted Tenet (2020), starring John David Washington, to be Hollywood's first major release after the shutdown, and he persuaded Warner Bros. not to send it to streaming. Originally set for July 17, the film was pushed to July 31, then to August 12, and finally opened on August 26, 2020, in 70 countries. It reached the United States on September 3, with theaters in New York and Los Angeles still closed. It grossed about US$ 365 million worldwide, only some US$ 58 million of it in the domestic market. Given the circumstances, it was not a flop, but it was not the rescue exhibitors had hoped for either. The studios pushed most of the big releases left on the 2020 calendar into the following year.

The year's tally was brutal. According to the Motion Picture Association, the global box office fell 72% in 2020, closing at US$ 12 billion, compared with more than US$ 40 billion the year before. In the United States and Canada, the drop was 80%. China, which reopened its theaters in July, grossed US$ 3 billion and, for the first time, overtook North America as the world's largest film market. In October, when Bond was delayed again, the chief executive of the British chain Cineworld, owner of Regal, called the decision “the final straw” and indefinitely closed all of its theaters in the U.S., the United Kingdom and Ireland, affecting 45,000 workers. In April 2021, the ArcLight and Pacific chains announced they would not reopen any of their locations, not even the historic Cinerama Dome in Hollywood. Cineworld would file for bankruptcy protection in September 2022, with debts of more than US$ 4.8 billion.

information.contentText: Christopher Nolan's time-bending spy film became the test case for the reopening of theaters in August 2020. It later won the Oscar for Best Visual Effects.

content_list.content_text: The first battle of the window wars was fought by colorful dolls. With theaters closed, Universal released Trolls World Tour (2020) on April 10, 2020, straight to digital rental in the United States, at $19.99, and the film brought in close to $100 million in three weeks. Buoyed by the result, NBCUniversal chief Jeff Shell told the Wall Street Journal that he planned to release films in both formats even after theaters reopened. The response came on April 28: AMC, the world's largest theater chain, announced it would no longer show any Universal films. The boycott lasted three months. At the end of July, the two companies made peace with a landmark deal: theatrical exclusivity, which had been about 90 days, dropped to 17, and the chain began receiving a share of digital revenue.

content_list.title: The window wars
content_list.description: The theatrical window is the period during which a film plays only in theaters before reaching audiences at home, whether on DVD, digital rental or streaming. It's what guarantees theaters' revenue: if a film comes to TV early, fewer people buy tickets. In 2019, the major chains demanded about 90 days of exclusivity. The pandemic brought down that wall in less than a year. In 2020, the deal between Universal and AMC created the 17-day window, or three weekends. Disney tested paid releases on Disney+, and Warner put an entire year of films on streaming the same day they opened in theaters. When exclusivity returned, it was shorter: in March 2021, Warner struck a deal with Cineworld for a 45-day window starting in 2022, and that period became an industry benchmark. In 2026, exhibitors were still negotiating every week: Universal guaranteed a minimum of five weekends in theaters, seven starting in 2027, and Paramount promised a 45-day window for its releases.

content_list.content_text: Disney chose a different path. Mulan (2020), the $200 million remake directed by Niki Caro, was scheduled for March 2020 and was postponed several times, until the company gave up on U.S. theaters. On September 4, the film premiered on Disney+ through Premier Access: on top of the subscription, viewers paid $29.99 to watch it. In countries without the service, such as China, it went to theaters, but grossed only about $70 million. In October, Disney announced that Soul (2020), by Pete Docter, would go straight to Disney+, at no extra cost, on Christmas Day 2020. The film won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature and would only reach U.S. theaters in January 2024, three and a half years later than planned.

information.contentText: Pixar's animated film about a music teacher who dreams of jazz was supposed to open in theaters in 2020. It ended up going straight to Disney+ at Christmas, a symbol of a year in which the living room replaced the movie theater.

content_list.content_text: The hardest blow came on December 3, 2020. Warner announced that all 17 of its 2021 films would open the same day in U.S. theaters and on HBO Max, where they would stay for a month, a plan nicknamed Project Popcorn. The model debuted with Wonder Woman 1984 (2020), by Patty Jenkins, on Christmas Day. Many filmmakers were not consulted. Nolan accused the studio of turning its directors into bait to lure subscribers and said the plan made no economic sense. Denis Villeneuve wrote in Variety that Warner might have just killed the Dune (2021) franchise. The film came out in October 2021 in theaters and on streaming at the same time, and even so, the sequel was green-lit.

quote.quote: They went to bed thinking they were working for the greatest movie studio and woke up to find out they were working for the worst streaming service.
quote.author: Christopher Nolan (to The Hollywood Reporter, 2020)

content_list.content_text: The most famous revolt, however, came from a star. On July 9, 2021, Black Widow (2021) opened simultaneously in theaters and on Disney+ Premier Access. On July 29, Scarlett Johansson sued Disney: part of her pay depended on the box office, and the simultaneous release, she argued, breached her contract and drained theaters. The company responded publicly that the actress had already been paid $20 million for the film. The case ended in a settlement on September 30, 2021, for an undisclosed amount. It was a watershed: it became clear that streaming was changing not only theaters but also how the people who make films get paid, a debate that would return in force in the 2023 Hollywood strikes.

information.contentTitle: Nomadland wins the Oscar for Best Picture
information.contentText: At the April 2021 ceremony, held at Los Angeles's Union Station, Nomadland completed a run that began with the Golden Lion in Venice, capping one of the strangest festival and awards seasons in history.

content_list.content_text: Even the Oscars changed their look. The 2021 ceremony was pushed back from February 28 to April 25, and for the first time films released only on streaming were eligible, as long as they had a planned theatrical release. The show left the Dolby Theatre and moved to Union Station, the Los Angeles train station, with a reduced audience. Nomadland, a quiet portrait of Americans who have lost their homes and live on the road, won Best Picture, Director and Actress, the last for Frances McDormand, her third Oscar in the category. Chloé Zhao became the second woman to win as director and the first woman of color. But the ceremony drew few viewers, in the hall and at home: with 10.4 million viewers in the U.S., it was the least-watched broadcast since record-keeping began.

information.contentText: Frances McDormand plays Fern, a widow who trades her house for a van and takes to the open road. Chloé Zhao's film won Best Picture, Director and Actress at the 2021 ceremony, held at Union Station.

content_list.content_text: The comeback only became clear at the end of 2021, when Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021), starring Tom Holland, opened exclusively in theaters, on December 16 in Brazil and the following day in the United States, and became the first film since the start of the pandemic to top US$ 1 billion. The old world, however, did not come back. The 90-day theatrical window gave way to windows of 17 to 45 days, and in early 2026 projections still put the global box office about 13% below its 2017–2019 average. In Brazil, by 2025, there were already more screens than in 2019, but far fewer moviegoers. It is in this shaken film industry that the rest of the decade begins: social media dictating success, horror as the safe bet, filmmakers coming from YouTube, the strikes and artificial intelligence, the strength of films from outside Hollywood, the streaming wars and the return of the event movie.

information.contentText: The meeting of three generations of the hero packed theaters in December 2021 and became proof that audiences would return to the movies for the right films.

movies.title: Tenet
movies.overview: Armado com apenas uma palavra – Tenet – e lutando pela sobrevivência do mundo inteiro, o Protagonista viaja através de um mundo crepuscular de espionagem internacional em uma missão que irá desenrolar em algo para além do tempo real.

movies.title: Nomadland
movies.overview: Após o colapso econômico de uma cidade na zona rural de Nevada, nos Estados Unidos, Fern, uma mulher de 60 anos, entra em sua van e parte para a estrada, vivendo uma vida fora da sociedade convencional como uma nômade moderna.

movies.title: Soul
movies.overview: Joe Gardner é um professor de música de ensino fundamental desanimado por não conseguir alcançar seu sonho de tocar no lendário clube de jazz The Blue Note, em Nova York. Quando um acidente o transporta para fora do seu corpo, fazendo com que ele exista em outra realidade na forma de sua alma, ele se vê forçado a embarcar em uma aventura ao lado da alma de uma criança que ainda está aprendendo sobre si, para aprender o que é necessário para retomar sua vida.

movies.title: Trolls 2
movies.overview: A rainha Poppy e Branch fazem uma descoberta surpreendente: há outros mundos Troll além do seu, e suas diferenças criam grandes confrontos entre essas diversas tribos. Quando uma ameaça misteriosa coloca todos os Trolls do país em perigo, Poppy, Branch e seu grupo de amigos devem embarcar em uma jornada épica para criar harmonia entre os Trolls rivais e uní-los contra um mal maior.

movies.title: Mulan
movies.overview: Hua Mulan é a espirituosa e determinada filha mais velha de um honrado guerreiro. Quando o Imperador da China emite um decreto que um homem de cada família deve servir no exército imperial, Mulan decide tomar o lugar de seu pai, que está doente. Assumindo a identidade de Hua Jun, ela se disfarça de homem para combater os invasores que estão atacando sua nação, provando-se uma grande guerreira.

movies.title: Mulher-Maravilha 1984
movies.overview: Em 1984, Diana Prince entra em conflito com dois inimigos formidáveis, Maxwell Lord e a Mulher-Leopardo, enquanto reencontra misteriosamente com seu antigo interesse amoroso Steve Trevor.

movies.title: Duna
movies.overview: Em um futuro distante, planetas são comandados por casas nobres que fazem parte de um império feudal intergalático. Paul Atreides é um jovem cuja família toma o controle do planeta deserto Arrakis, também conhecido como Duna. A única fonte da especiaria Melange, a substância mais importante do cosmos, Arrakis se mostra ser um planeta nem um pouco fácil de governar.

movies.title: Viúva Negra
movies.overview: Natasha Romanoff, também conhecida como Viúva Negra, confronta o lado mais sombrio de sua história quando surge uma perigosa conspiração ligada ao seu passado. Perseguida por uma força implacável disposta a tudo para destruí-la, Natasha precisa agora lidar com seu passado como espiã e com as relações que deixou para trás muito antes de se tornar uma Vingadora.

movies.title: 007: Sem Tempo para Morrer
movies.overview: Bond deixou o serviço ativo e está desfrutando de uma vida tranquila na Jamaica. Sua paz é interrompida quando o seu velho amigo Felix Leiter, da CIA, aparece pedindo sua ajuda. A missão de resgatar um cientista sequestrado acaba sendo muito mais difícil do que o esperado, deixando Bond no caminho de um vilão misterioso e armado com uma nova tecnologia perigosa.

movies.title: Homem-Aranha: Sem Volta Para Casa
movies.overview: Peter Parker é desmascarado e não consegue mais separar sua vida normal dos grandes riscos de ser um super-herói. Quando ele pede ajuda ao Doutor Estranho, os riscos se tornam ainda mais perigosos, e o forçam a descobrir o que realmente significa ser o Homem-Aranha...

content_list.title: Timeline of Events from 2020 to Today
content_list.description: The pandemic shuts down theaters, streaming consolidates, Hollywood grinds to a halt with strikes and world cinema rises to the top. Click here to see the main events in cinema from 2020 to today in chronological order.
